brief.deck: Baseten, the inference platform behind Cursor, Abridge and Lovable, announced a $1.5B Series F on 22 June in two tranches at $13B and $11B, led by Altimeter, Conviction and Spark Capital. It is the fourth raise in 18 months for a company whose revenue grew 20x in a year.
brief.the_case_p1: Baseten's own release of 22 June puts the numbers on record: $1.5B across two tranches at $13B and $11B, co-led by Sands Capital and Wellington, with Greylock, IVP, Battery and D.E. Shaw Ventures behind them; more than $2B raised in total. The price has moved from $2.15B in September 2025 to $5B in January to $13B now. The platform serves more than 1 billion inference calls a day across 87 clusters on 18 clouds, revenue grew 20x in a year, and headcount is to triple in 2026 as the company builds an enterprise sales motion.
brief.the_case_p2: That last point is the opening. A developer-led brand that must now sell to CIOs needs a stage its rivals already occupy: CoreWeave took Aston Martin Aramco's AI cloud seat in May 2025 and Core Scientific sits on Cadillac's car. Baseten is the inference layer that runs on those clouds, not one of them, and it has no seat.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Series F was announced on 22 June and brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise. Austin in late October and Las Vegas in November are the US stages left in 2026, and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Haas is the American team with the leanest engineering operation on the grid, backed since 2026 by Toyota Gazoo Racing as title and technical partner. Its technology roster is Mphasis, CommScope, Ruckus and Infobip; there is no cloud, GPU or AI-inference partner, so the lane is clean. A team that buys engineering capacity rather than building it is the natural first customer for compute you do not own; Austin is its home race.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO TGR HAAS F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. The models a team trains (strategy and tyre-degradation, computer vision on pit-lane and onboard video, telemetry anomaly detection) must be served at race weekends at low latency and at a cost a small team can carry. Baseten runs them from cloud regions near each circuit with autoscaling, so Haas gets an inference layer under Toyota's data without buying GPUs. In return: Official AI Inference Partner, livery, US-race hospitality.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official AI Inference Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the enterprise build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: sidepod placement, naming of the team's model-serving environment, US-race hospitality, engineering content with the Toyota programme.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Srivastava co-founded Baseten in San Francisco in 2019 with Amir Haghighat (CTO), Philip Howes (Chief Scientist) and Pankaj Gupta, and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Matt Slagle, Chief Revenue Officer, who owns the enterprise motion. No CMO or CFO is listed.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Tuhin, you have raised $1.5B to sell inference to enterprises, and CoreWeave already bought the Aston Martin seat to sell them compute. The American team has an open AI lane and its home race in October. 25 minutes before Austin to see how it prices?”
score_cells: Round announced 22 Jun; Austin and Las Vegas in window.
$1.5B raise at $13B; more than $2B raised in total.
Developer brand turning enterprise; B2B infrastructure.
Enterprise push and hiring; no hard deadline beyond Q4.
MODE A: serving the team's models at race weekends.
risks: Baseten reports growth multiples, not revenue; Sacra's ~$600M annualised figure is an outside estimate.
Anchor on the announced round and named customers; ask for the enterprise revenue mix on the first call.
CoreWeave, Core Scientific, Oracle, Microsoft and Google Cloud all carry AI or cloud messaging; another infrastructure logo can read as a follower.
Position inference, not compute, as the category, and Haas as the team whose engineering budget it changes most.
brief.bottom_line: A $1.5B raise at $13B, a fourth round in 18 months and a stated pivot to enterprise selling put Baseten at peak brand-investment authority. The AI lane at Haas is open, the workstream is real, and two US races remain inside the window.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 22 June 2026 Baseten announced a $1.5B Series F in two tranches at $13B and $11B valuations, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction and Spark Capital and co-led by Sands Capital and Wellington Management, with Battery Ventures, Blackbird, D.E. Shaw Ventures, Durable Capital, Greylock, IVP, Verified Capital and 01A. Total raised now exceeds $2B (company release).

why_now.label: Six times the price in nine months
why_now.text: BOND led $150M at $2.15B in September 2025; IVP and CapitalG led $300M at $5B in January 2026; the June financing prices the company at up to $13B. Four raises in 18 months is a company that expects to be much larger, and public, soon.

why_now.label: From developers to enterprises
why_now.text: The release says headcount will triple in 2026 to meet enterprise demand, and the customer list (Abridge, Clay, Cursor, Lovable, Mercor, OpenEvidence) is AI-native companies rather than large enterprises. Selling to CIOs is a brand problem, which is what a Formula 1 partnership is for. Sacra estimates annualised revenue at about $600M as of March 2026; that is an estimate, not a company figure.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the US rounds left in 2026, and teams close their 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced at the American team's home race and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: TGR Haas F1 Team carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner with Mphasis (digital), CommScope (connectivity), Ruckus and Infobip on the technology side. No cloud, GPU or AI-inference partner: Official AI Inference Partner is a clean category at the lowest team-partner price on the grid.

why_team.label: A team that buys capacity
why_team.text: Haas runs the leanest engineering operation in Formula 1 and has always bought what others build, from Ferrari power units to Toyota's design and manufacturing services. An inference platform that removes the need to own GPUs is the same trade: capacity without capital.

why_team.label: American team, American company
why_team.text: Haas is the only US-owned team; Baseten is a San Francisco company entering enterprise sales in the US market. Austin is the team's home race and the natural announcement stage; Las Vegas and Miami follow.

why_team.label: Precedent without conflict
why_team.text: The grid has priced the archetype (CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Core Scientific at Cadillac) but those are clouds. Baseten runs on 18 clouds; it competes with none of the team's existing partners and would sit alongside Toyota's technical programme rather than under a hyperscaler's brand.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Serving the team's trained models at race weekends: race-strategy and tyre-degradation models, computer vision on pit-lane and onboard video, telemetry anomaly detection. Baseten hosts them from cloud regions near each circuit with autoscaling, so latency and cost fit a small team's weekend.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner selling to CIOs and AI-native founders brings a guest list of enterprise buyers and investors to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's B2B partners (Mphasis, CommScope, Infobip) want in the suite.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: Co-produced engineering content on how a small team uses AI at the track; a reference customer for Baseten's enterprise sales; a developer programme around the team's public data that reaches Baseten's core audience.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official AI Inference Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the model-serving environment, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, driver and engineering access for Baseten's channels.

ruled_out.reason: CoreWeave, Official AI Cloud Computing Partner since May 2025, owns the AI infrastructure lane.
Core Scientific and TWG AI occupy the compute and AI lanes.
Oracle is title partner and cloud incumbent.
Microsoft holds the cloud lane at both.
Google Cloud and Dell occupy cloud and hardware.
HP (title) and IBM cover compute and cloud services.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise on the roster; lane crowded.
Claude is Official Thinking Partner and VAST the data platform; the AI lane there is defined by Anthropic, and a second AI infrastructure brand would sit under it.
Open (Dynatrace, Confluent, Siemens) and a credible second choice, but it is the Red Bull group's second team under Oracle's title relationship at the senior team.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Tuhin Srivastava before the US GP in Austin to test the enterprise-brand need, size an Official AI Inference Partner entry against TGR Haas F1 Team's 2027 roster, and agree an Austin announcement window.

# Baseten → TGR Haas F1 Team — verification log (N° 184, issued for 22 Jun 2026)

Built in-session on 6 Sep 2026 at no API cost, in rebuild mode for the desk row dated 22 Jun 2026. The thin row read 87/100 with no team; this case scores **76/100 HOT** and points at **TGR Haas F1 Team**.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** businesswire.com, baseten.co, finance.yahoo.com, morningstar.com, bloomberg.com and haasf1team.com were egress-blocked. TechCrunch had reported the raise on 18 Jun 2026; the company confirmed it on the 22nd. The thin row's source (letsdatascience.com) was an aggregator; replaced with the release.
